title: RemoteAccessStats
description: Statistics for a Foxglove remote access gateway. Counters are cumulative over the lifetime of the gateway.

state.description: The gateway's connection to the Foxglove platform. 'connected' means the gateway is available for remote access, whether or not a viewer session is active. 'shutting_down' is reported in the last message, after the gateway is stopped.

session_active.description: Whether the gateway is joined to a remote access session, which happens when a viewer requests a connection.

viewer_count.description: The number of viewers connected to the current session, or 0 if no session is active.

rtt_ms.description: The most recent ICE round-trip time between the gateway and the remote access server, in milliseconds. It is sampled every 30 seconds during a session, and is omitted if no session is active or the session has not been sampled yet.

connection_quality.description: The remote access server's estimate of the quality of the gateway's connection. Omitted if no session is active.

reconnects.description: The number of times the gateway lost its connection to the Foxglove platform and started reconnecting.

participant_resets.description: The number of times a viewer was disconnected and reconnected because its control message queue overflowed or a write to it failed.

data_track_full.description: Messages dropped because a data track's send queue was full. Viewers also see these as gaps in the channel's sequence numbers.

data_track_not_ready.description: Messages dropped because a channel's data track was not published. This is expected for a few milliseconds after each channel is advertised, so it is not broken down by topic.

oversized.description: Messages dropped because they exceeded the maximum data track message size.

video_queue.description: Image messages dropped before video encoding because the encoder was slower than the log rate.

point_cloud_queue.description: Point cloud messages dropped before compression because compression was slower than the log rate.

video_encode_errors.description: Image messages that could not be encoded as video, for example because they could not be decoded or were below the minimum encoder size.

topics.description: Drop counters for each topic with at least one nonzero counter, for every cause except data_track_not_ready. The counters for each topic add up to the gateway-wide counters of the same name.

data_track_full.description: Messages dropped because the data track's send queue was full.

oversized.description: Messages dropped because they exceeded the maximum data track message size.

video_queue.description: Image messages dropped before video encoding.

point_cloud_queue.description: Point cloud messages dropped before compression.

video_encode_errors.description: Image messages that could not be encoded as video.
